criteria.statement: Only signed-in public sector staff and administrators may create an opportunity; a request from a vendor or an anonymous visitor is refused.
criteria.given: a visitor who is not signed in, or is signed in as a vendor
criteria.when: they attempt to create an opportunity
criteria.then: the request is refused and no opportunity is created

criteria.statement: A published opportunity whose proposal deadline has passed closes on its own: it moves to the first evaluation stage of its program, every proposal submitted against it moves to review, and its author is notified that it is ready for evaluation.
criteria.given: a published opportunity whose proposal deadline has passed
criteria.when: the service next handles any request
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to its program's first evaluation stage with the note "This opportunity has closed.", its submitted proposals move to review, and its author receives a notification
notes: closure is driven by ordinary traffic rather than a clock, throttled so it runs at most once a minute, and additionally attached to the health-check route so that it still runs when the site is idle. An opportunity therefore closes at the first request after its deadline, not at the deadline itself.

criteria.statement: Every opportunity belongs to exactly one of three procurement programs — Code With Us, Sprint With Us or Team With Us — chosen when it is created and never changed afterwards.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating a new opportunity
criteria.when: they choose a program and complete creation
criteria.then: the opportunity is filed under that program and offers only that program's fields, stages and actions
notes: the running code implements three programs, but the application's own README describes only Code With Us and Sprint With Us, and its generated database-schema document lists no Team With Us tables at all. Both documents predate Team With Us; a human should confirm that all three programs carry forward rather than assuming the documents are merely stale.

criteria.statement: An anonymous visitor or a vendor sees only opportunities that have been published; drafts and opportunities under review are not listed to them and cannot be opened by them.
criteria.given: an opportunity in draft or under review
criteria.when: an anonymous visitor or a vendor lists opportunities, or opens that opportunity's address directly
criteria.then: the opportunity does not appear in the list, and opening it directly reports that it was not found

criteria.statement: An opportunity saved as a draft is accepted with incomplete content, and any missing or invalid dates are defaulted to fourteen days ahead.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff filling in a new opportunity
criteria.when: they save it as a draft with fields still blank
criteria.then: the draft is stored, no content validation error is raised, and absent dates are set to fourteen days from the day of saving

criteria.statement: A member of public sector staff sees every published opportunity plus their own drafts and opportunities under review, and an administrator sees every opportunity.
criteria.given: two members of public sector staff, each with an unpublished opportunity of their own
criteria.when: each lists opportunities
criteria.then: each sees their own unpublished opportunity and not the other's, while an administrator listing opportunities sees both

criteria.statement: An opportunity that is not a draft is rejected unless it carries a title of 1 to 200 characters, a teaser of at most 500 characters, a location, and a description of 1 to 10,000 characters.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit it with a missing title, a title over 200 characters, a teaser over 500 characters, a missing location, or a description that is missing or over 10,000 characters
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the offending field is named in the response

criteria.statement: Every change to an opportunity's content creates a new version of it and records an edit in its history; the opportunity always shows its most recent version.
criteria.given: a published opportunity
criteria.when: an administrator changes its description and saves
criteria.then: the opportunity shows the new description, its history gains an entry recording that it was edited, by whom and when, and the previous content is retained

criteria.statement: An opportunity that is not a draft must state whether remote work is acceptable, and must carry a remote-work description of up to 500 characters whenever remote work is acceptable.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they mark it as accepting remote work but leave the remote-work description empty
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: when remote work is not acceptable the remote-work description may be empty, and any value over 500 characters is rejected either way.

criteria.statement: Any signed-in person may watch an opportunity they did not create, may stop watching it, and cannot watch the same opportunity twice.
criteria.given: a signed-in person viewing an opportunity created by somebody else and not yet watched by them
criteria.when: they choose to watch it, and then choose to watch it again
criteria.then: the first request records them as watching it and the second is refused as a duplicate
notes: a person is refused when they try to watch their own opportunity, with the message "You cannot subscribe to your own opportunity."

criteria.statement: A Code With Us opportunity must offer a reward of at least $1 and at most $70,000, and must name at least one skill.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Code With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a reward outside $1 to $70,000, or submit no skills
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: duplicate skills are silently collapsed rather than rejected.

criteria.statement: Opening an opportunity's public page counts as a view of that opportunity.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been viewed a known number of times
criteria.when: anyone, signed in or not, opens its public page
criteria.then: the recorded view count for that opportunity increases by one

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us opportunity must state a total maximum budget of at least $1 and at most $5,000,000, while a Team With Us opportunity must state a maximum budget of at least $1 with no upper limit.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a Sprint With Us budget above $5,000,000, or any budget below $1
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: the absence of an upper budget limit on Team With Us is a difference from the other two programs, not a stated policy; nothing in the application explains it, so a human should rule on whether it carries forward.

criteria.statement: An opportunity's key dates must run in order — the proposal deadline no earlier than today, then the assignment date, then the start date, then the completion date — and each date is recorded as 4:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day chosen.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a proposal deadline in the past, or any later date that falls before the date preceding it
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: when an already-published opportunity's deadline has passed, an edit is measured against that past deadline instead of today, so a closed opportunity can be edited without its dates being forced forward.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity is rejected unless its evaluation weights total exactly one hundred per cent.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit weights that do not total one hundred per cent
criteria.then: the submission is rejected with a message saying the scoring weights must total 100%
notes: Sprint With Us weights four stages (questions, code challenge, team scenario, price); Team With Us weights three (questions, challenge, price). Each individual weight is separately required to fall between 0 and 100.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us opportunity must have an implementation phase, and may only have an inception phase if it also has a prototype phase.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Sprint With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they include an inception phase but no prototype phase
criteria.then: the submission is rejected with a message saying a prototype phase must follow an inception phase

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity must name an evaluation panel of at least two distinct public sector employees, with at most one of them marked as chair.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity
criteria.when: they submit fewer than two panel members, the same person twice, more than one chair, or anyone who is not a public sector employee
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the reason is named
notes: the rule as written in the application's own comment says "one and only one chair", but the code accepts a panel with no chair at all and rejects only a second chair. A human should rule on which was intended.

criteria.statement: Each evaluation question on a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity carries a question, a guideline, a maximum score, a response word limit and a position, and an optional minimum score that must be lower than the question's maximum score.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff adding an evaluation question to an opportunity
criteria.when: they submit a question or guideline outside 1 to 1,000 characters, a score below 1, a word limit outside 1 to 3,000, a position outside 0 to 100, or a minimum score equal to or above the question's score
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the offending field is named
notes: the same limits apply to Sprint With Us "team questions" and Team With Us "resource questions"; the two differ only in name.

criteria.statement: Each resource on a Team With Us opportunity names one service area and a target allocation between 1 and 100 per cent of full time.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Team With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a resource with a target allocation outside 1 to 100, or a service area that is not one of the five recognised areas
criteria.then: the submission is rejected

criteria.statement: An opportunity moves through the states draft, under review, published, one or more program-specific evaluation stages, processing, and finally awarded or cancelled.
criteria.given: any opportunity
criteria.when: its state is read at any point in its life
criteria.then: the state is one of the values recognised for its program, and no other value is accepted by the store
notes: Code With Us has a single evaluation stage; Sprint With Us has four (team questions individual, team questions consensus, code challenge, team scenario); Team With Us has three (resource questions individual, resource questions consensus, challenge).

criteria.statement: An opportunity may only change state along the permitted path for its program, and a request for any other change is refused.
criteria.given: an opportunity in a given state
criteria.when: someone requests a change to a state that is not reachable from it — for example from draft straight to an evaluation stage, or out of an awarded or cancelled opportunity
criteria.then: the request is refused and the opportunity's state is unchanged
notes: a draft may go to under review or straight to published; under review may only go to published; published and every evaluation stage may go to the next stage or to cancelled; awarded and cancelled are final.

criteria.statement: Submitting a draft opportunity for review is refused unless the opportunity is complete, and the person is told the opportunity is incomplete rather than which field is missing.
criteria.given: a draft opportunity with a field still blank
criteria.when: its author submits it for review
criteria.then: the request is refused with a message saying the opportunity is incomplete and asking the author to complete and save the form
notes: Code With Us checks only title, teaser, remote-work fields, location and description at this point, while Sprint With Us additionally checks budget, skills, weights and every phase — so a Code With Us opportunity can reach "under review" with a missing reward or missing skills and be caught only at publication.

criteria.statement: Only an administrator may publish an opportunity.
criteria.given: an opportunity in draft or under review
criteria.when: a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator asks to publish it
criteria.then: the request is refused and the opportunity stays unpublished

criteria.statement: Publishing an opportunity records the moment of publication, which is thereafter shown as the opportunity's published date.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been published
criteria.when: anyone views it
criteria.then: the date shown as its publication date is the moment of the first publication, even if it was later republished

criteria.statement: On closing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity, each submitted proposal is given an anonymous proponent name for use during evaluation.
criteria.given: a published Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity with submitted proposals
criteria.when: it closes at its proposal deadline
criteria.then: each submitted proposal is labelled "Proponent 1", "Proponent 2" and so on
notes: Code With Us does not anonymise proponents.

criteria.statement: An opportunity moves to processing on its own once every proposal still in contention has been scored at its program's final evaluation stage.
criteria.given: an opportunity at its final evaluation stage with at least one proposal still in contention
criteria.when: the last of those proposals is scored
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to processing and the change is recorded with a note saying it was moved automatically because all proposals have been evaluated

criteria.statement: Awarding a proposal moves its opportunity to awarded and records the winning proponent against it; every other proposal still in contention is marked not awarded.
criteria.given: an opportunity in processing with proposals against it
criteria.when: an administrator awards one of those proposals
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to awarded, the winning proponent is recorded against it, and the remaining proposals are marked not awarded

criteria.statement: An awarded opportunity shows its successful proponent's name to everyone, and shows the proponent's contact details and score only to those permitted to see the proposal's score.
criteria.given: an awarded opportunity
criteria.when: a visitor who may not see proposal scores views it
criteria.then: the successful proponent's name is shown and their contact details and score are withheld

criteria.statement: Only an administrator may cancel an opportunity, and only once it has been published.
criteria.given: an opportunity that is published or at any evaluation stage or in processing
criteria.when: an administrator cancels it, giving an optional note of up to 1,000 characters
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to cancelled and stops accepting proposals
notes: a draft or under-review opportunity cannot be cancelled — it is deleted instead.

criteria.statement: An opportunity may be deleted only while it is a draft or under review, and only by an administrator or, for a draft, by the member of public sector staff who created it.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been published at any point
criteria.when: anyone asks to delete it
criteria.then: the request is refused and the opportunity remains
notes: the application's own interface documentation says deletion is permitted only for a draft, while the code also permits an administrator to delete an opportunity that is under review. The three programs also disagree with each other: for Code With Us and Sprint With Us the creating staff member may delete only a draft, but for Team With Us they may also delete one that is under review. A human should rule on the intended rule before it is carried forward.

criteria.statement: The names of the people who created and last changed an opportunity are shown only to administrators and to those people themselves.
criteria.given: a published opportunity
criteria.when: it is viewed by someone who is neither an administrator nor the person who created or last changed it
criteria.then: the creating and changing people's names are absent from what is shown

criteria.statement: An opportunity's administrator and its author can see its full change history, how many times it has been viewed, how many people are watching it and how many proposals have been submitted; nobody else can.
criteria.given: a published opportunity that has been viewed, watched and proposed against
criteria.when: its author or an administrator opens it
criteria.then: they see its history of state changes and events and its counts of views, watchers and submitted proposals
notes: the reporting counts are withheld while the opportunity is still a draft or under review, even from the author.

criteria.statement: Public sector staff cannot see the proposals submitted against an opportunity until it has left the published state.
criteria.given: a published opportunity that has received proposals
criteria.when: its author or an administrator asks to see the proposals
criteria.then: the request is refused until the opportunity has closed and moved to an evaluation stage

criteria.statement: An addendum of 1 to 5,000 characters may be added to any opportunity that is no longer a draft, by an administrator or by the staff member who created it, and cannot be removed afterwards.
criteria.given: a published opportunity
criteria.when: its author adds an addendum
criteria.then: the addendum is appended to the opportunity with its author and date, an entry is added to the opportunity's history, and there is no action that removes it

criteria.statement: An administrator or an opportunity's author may attach a private note, with files, to a Code With Us or Sprint With Us opportunity's history at any point in its life.
criteria.given: a Code With Us or Sprint With Us opportunity in any state
criteria.when: its author adds a note of up to 1,000 characters with attachments
criteria.then: the note and its attachments appear in the opportunity's history, which only the author and administrators can see
notes: Team With Us offers no such action at all. Nothing in the application explains the omission, so a human should decide whether it is a gap to close or a deliberate difference.

criteria.statement: Publishing an opportunity notifies everyone who has asked for new-opportunity notifications, and separately confirms the publication to the opportunity's author.
criteria.given: an opportunity ready to be published and people who have turned notifications on
criteria.when: an administrator publishes it
criteria.then: each of those people receives a notice that a new opportunity has been posted, and the opportunity's author receives a confirmation

criteria.statement: Changing or adding an addendum to an opportunity that is neither a draft nor cancelled notifies everyone watching it, everyone who has submitted a proposal to it, and its author.
criteria.given: a published opportunity with watchers and submitted proposals
criteria.when: an administrator edits it or adds an addendum
criteria.then: its watchers, its proponents and its author are each notified once
notes: nobody is notified when the opportunity is a draft or has been cancelled.

criteria.statement: Cancelling an opportunity notifies everyone watching it and everyone who has submitted a proposal to it, and separately notifies its author.
criteria.given: a published opportunity with watchers and submitted proposals
criteria.when: an administrator cancels it
criteria.then: its watchers and proponents are told it has been cancelled, and its author is told separately that the cancellation was actioned

criteria.statement: Submitting an opportunity for review notifies every administrator, and confirms the submission to its author.
criteria.given: a complete draft opportunity
criteria.when: its author submits it for review
criteria.then: every administrator is notified that an opportunity awaits review, and the author receives a confirmation

criteria.statement: The opportunity list groups opportunities into unpublished, open and closed, showing open opportunities with the nearest proposal deadline first, closed ones most recently closed first, and unpublished ones most recently changed first.
criteria.given: a set of opportunities in a mix of states
criteria.when: someone opens the opportunity list
criteria.then: each opportunity appears in exactly one of the three groups, ordered as described
notes: an opportunity counts as open only while it is published and its proposal deadline is still in the future; everything published and past its deadline, including cancelled and awarded opportunities, counts as closed.

criteria.statement: The opportunity list can be narrowed by program, by state, to remote-friendly opportunities only, and by free text matched against title and location.
criteria.given: a list of opportunities across all three programs
criteria.when: someone selects a program, selects a state, ticks remote-only, or types words into the search box
criteria.then: only opportunities matching every chosen condition remain visible
notes: the state filter offers draft, under review, published, evaluation and awarded; there is no option for opportunities in processing or cancelled, so those can only be found by clearing the filter.

criteria.statement: Only an administrator can open the full report of a completed opportunity, which shows the opportunity, its addenda, its history and every proposal in one continuous document.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been evaluated
criteria.when: a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator opens its report address
criteria.then: they are refused, while an administrator opening the same address sees the whole record in one document

criteria.statement: Advancing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity out of the consensus stage is refused unless every consensus evaluation has been submitted and at least one proponent has met the minimum score on every question that sets one.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity at the questions consensus stage
criteria.when: its author asks to move it on while a consensus is unsubmitted, or while no proponent has cleared every question's minimum score
criteria.then: the request is refused and the reason is named

criteria.statement: Advancing a Sprint With Us opportunity to the team scenario stage is refused unless every proponent in the code challenge has been scored or disqualified and at least one remains screened in.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity at the code challenge stage
criteria.when: its author asks to move it to the team scenario stage while a proponent is unscored and not disqualified
criteria.then: the request is refused with a message saying all proponents must be scored first

criteria.statement: The evaluation panel of a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity may be changed only while the opportunity is a draft, under review, published, or at the first questions stage.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity that has reached the consensus stage or beyond
criteria.when: its author asks to change the evaluation panel
criteria.then: the request is refused and the panel stays as it was

criteria.statement: A member of public sector staff who is not an administrator can publish a Code With Us opportunity directly, by creating it as published rather than by publishing an existing one.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator
criteria.when: they create a Code With Us opportunity with its state set to published
criteria.then: the opportunity is created and published, and the subscriber notifications for a published opportunity are sent
notes: this contradicts the administrator-only publication rule recovered as D-opportunities-17. The equivalent Sprint With Us and Team With Us creation checks refuse this case explicitly, so the Code With Us omission reads as an oversight rather than an intended difference. There is no replacement criterion because the corrected behaviour is already stated by D-opportunities-17; a human should rule on whether the rebuild simply closes the hole.

criteria.statement: A Team With Us opportunity in processing can be awarded, even though the recorded set of permitted state changes does not include that step.
criteria.given: a Team With Us opportunity in processing
criteria.when: an administrator awards one of its proposals
criteria.then: the opportunity becomes awarded
notes: the permitted-change table for Team With Us allows only cancellation out of processing, while the equivalent tables for the other two programs allow the award. Awarding does not consult that table, so the award succeeds anyway. Whether the table or the award path is wrong cannot be determined from the application; a human should rule.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity can be moved out of its consensus stage by a second, older action that does not check whether the consensus evaluations have been submitted.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity at the questions consensus stage with consensus evaluations still unsubmitted
criteria.when: its author uses the older "start code challenge" action rather than the newer "finalize consensuses" action
criteria.then: the opportunity advances to the code challenge stage without the consensus check being applied
notes: the application marks the Sprint With Us version of this action as deprecated in a comment but still accepts it; the Team With Us equivalent carries no such comment. There is no replacement criterion because the intended guard is already stated by D-opportunities-43; a human should rule on removing the older path.

criteria.statement: The author of a published opportunity, who is not an administrator, can change its details.
criteria.given: a published opportunity created by a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator
criteria.when: that person submits a change to its details
criteria.then: the change is accepted and a new version is recorded
notes: the interface offers the edit only to administrators once an opportunity is published, but the underlying service accepts it from the author too. The two disagree, and nothing in the application says which is intended.

criteria.statement: "Suspended" remains a permitted stored state for an opportunity although no action can put an opportunity into it.
criteria.given: the set of states an opportunity may hold
criteria.when: any state change is attempted
criteria.then: no path leads to the suspended state, and no listing, filter or transition treats it as reachable
notes: the state is named "deprecated suspended" in the application's own code but is still accepted by the store's constraint, so historical records may hold it. There is no replacement criterion: whether the rebuild must still display an opportunity left in this state from the old data is a question for a human, not something the application answers.

criteria.statement: The application's published interface description for opportunities is incomplete: it omits the Team With Us program entirely, omits the "submit for review" and "add note" actions, and describes only two of the three states an opportunity may be created in.
criteria.given: someone reading the application's own interface description to learn what an opportunity supports
criteria.when: they compare it against what the service actually accepts
criteria.then: they find actions and states the description does not mention, and no description at all for one of the three programs
notes: recorded so that the gap is not mistaken for absent behaviour by a later reader. The behaviours themselves are stated in the criteria above; this criterion is about the documentation being an unreliable second source, which is why several criteria here are graded on code alone.
